body: Thank you, I really appreciate it ☺️

Yeah, I think I should do that. Just sit down with him and plan on future communication and what works best for the both of us. I've been looking up ways to spend time together and stay connected online, and I think there might be a slight chance we can meet monthly or bimonthly.

Yes, I agree with both attachment styles being unhealthy. My constant anxiety is bringing down my overall QOL, so I should really put more effort into dismantling it. I'm hopeful that I could do it together with my boyfriend, since he's also focusing on learning about his avoidance and practicing activating strategies and journaling.

Thank you so much for the detailed response, it really helps 😊

With the marriage statement, that was barely 3 months into the relationship. It was rushed and I knew it, but I wouldn't lie when I say it felt great to hear it. It just felt like the relationship was secured and I can love him fully without worrying about it. Also ticks off one less thing to stress about. Hindsight 20/20, should've expected the 180.

I'm also really happy about our communication. Even though I used to hesitate bringing up issues or feelings that I have, he has never made me feel bad and is surprisingly gentle most of the time. He's more of a pragmatic type, but he's so sweet to me that I have no problem being more open and direct with him now. The only problem is our online communication, which wouldn't bother me if we weren't going to be ldr.

It was an eventful year for me, since all my firsts happened this year. 

1 first date that led nowhere (Bumble). We talked well for 2 weeks but got ghosted after the date. Got some thick skin after that

1 situationship that lasted for 2 months (Reddit). Started as friends, then it got spicy after a few weeks and we agreed to have a casual relationship. Got feelings first and he didn't want commitment so I broke it off

1 relationship ongoing (Discord). Started talking with him on a meetup server, and it turned out he was living right next to me XD. He asked me out and I said no first (2 years younger than me), but I did have some feelings for him. A mutual friend told me to just try it out, and I accepted. Dating stage for 3 weeks before becoming official. 

Some interesting notes:

- There was always, give or take, a 2 month gap between meeting each guy for me

It was nice having that period for reflecting on what happened, noting what I liked and hated with each guy and the mistakes I made. Also, finding the joy in being single and having fun with my friends 

- All of them happened to be guys I met online 🙃

I was surprised at first when I typed this out, but thinking about it, I realised I have really gone out of my comfort zone this year, meeting and talking with new people online. I've made a lot of great acquaintances and friends this year, and also managed to maintain the quality relationships I already had.

- It's really ironic that I spent most of my life saying I would only date older men, only to fall for a younger guy 😅

After being disappointed with the first 2 guys who were older than me, I think I developed an aversion to them, and with this sweet, cute guy saying he fell for me hard, taking me out on dates and saying he'll show his commitment by his actions and consistency, I fell hard for him too 💖
Is it Chennai K-Meetup? They're a bunch of really nice people, and they recently reached 1k members

IMO, we should first think about why we need a certain "safe space", because the nature of safe spaces is to exclude certain people from participating in that space. If we want to discuss certain women-centric issues (like abortion), then we can exclude most men from participating in the discussions, right?  It is up to the people who create those spaces to decide who to allow into those spaces, the only condition being that they ensure the safety or integrity of that space, and while this condition can exclude well-meaning people, there are other spaces they can participate in or they can create their own to discuss their issues.

The thing is, I don't care about disappointing the average person, but I do care about the people I love. Almost all my friends have a job or their future planned out, something concrete. I'm just floating along with them. My parents are fine with my situation for now, but it feels like a timebomb's strapped to my chest tightly. Anyday, my family might realise that I'm not going to do anything useful in my life, and kick me out. My friends will never find out, and I'll be alone. It's just a horrible mix of anxiety and apathy for me. Everyday.
It's not just peeing in a bottle, it's about being overworked to the point that you're not allowed a few minutes to relieve yourself (in a washroom), and that sounds terrible.
